caller_turns: I am cleaning an old camping lantern at my kitchen table. The glass is cloudy and I keep leaving fingerprints on it.
It belonged to my aunt Belen. She used to take it fishing, although she rarely caught anything. I like that it has been useful to somebody.
I have taken the glass out now. There is a dead moth inside. That must have been an ambitious last evening.
I am making tea while it dries. Do you keep old things because you like them, or only because they still work?
I volunteer at a little lending library on Wednesdays. Today I am sorting a box of returned books and someone has used a bus ticket as a bookmark.
The ticket is for a town called Alderford. I have never been there. I like finding small things people leave behind, provided it is not food.
My friend Neri says we should display the odd bookmarks by the desk. Last month somebody left a pressed fern in an atlas.
There is a thunderstorm outside now and nobody has come in for an hour. I am eating a pear behind the desk. What do you do with a quiet afternoon?

I have just noticed a little dent on the base. I made that dent when I was eleven and denied it for years. She probably knew.
The tea has gone cold because I forgot about it. I suppose the lantern is receiving better care than I am giving my lunch.
I have put the glass back in. The lantern is going on a shelf until our next camping trip. I am pleased with a very small accomplishment.
